ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Stan had 125 small cubes. He glued some of them together to form a large cube with nine tunnels, each perpendicular to two opposite faces and passing through the cube, as shown in the diagram. How many of the small cubes did he not use?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a large cube whose visible faces are divided into a 5 by 5 grid of small cube faces, so the full cube is 5 by 5 by 5. The picture shows tunnel openings on the top, front, and right faces. On each of these visible faces, the openings occur in three matching diagonal positions, which can be labeled 2, 3, and 4 in the face grid. Reasoning: Since 125 = 5^3, the original 125 small cubes would make a complete 5 by 5 by 5 cube. There are nine tunnels total: three tunnels in each of the three perpendicular directions. Each tunnel passes straight through the cube and would remove 5 small cubes, so a naive count gives 9 × 5 = 45 removed cubes. However, some removed cubes are counted more than once where tunnels intersect. For each of the three matching diagonal positions, one tunnel from each of the three directions meets at the same cube. Thus there are 3 groups of triple intersections. In each group, the three tunnels create 3 pairwise overlaps, so across all groups there are 3 × 3 = 9 pairwise overlaps. Inclusion-exclusion gives removed cubes = 45 - 9 + 3 = 39. These removed cubes are exactly the small cubes Stan did not use. Final answer: 39
